items.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
items.summary_1line: A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility...
items.editor_note: Latest: replaces similarity search with utility scoring across the full memory pool.

editorial.tldr: This is a loose cluster of mostly arXiv research on agent memory and context, not one event. Since late October, papers have proposed graph and transition-aware memory, while InfoQ and an arXiv paper argued that context should be engineered as infrastructure.
editorial.whats_new: Jetriever (Nov 16) ranks stored agent memories by a model's usefulness score for the current question instead of embedding similarity.
editorial.why_it_matters: Several papers report that similarity-only retrieval misses what agents need: evolving facts, multi-hop links, and memories that do not resemble the query.
editorial.take_for_builders: Add eval cases where the useful memory does not resemble the query or a fact has changed over time, and check whether your similarity-only retriever misses them before adopting a new memory design.

beats.headline: Graph and time-aware memory to keep identity and change history
beats.summary: Papers model memory as registries, knowledge graphs, and preference transitions instead of flat chunks.

beats.headline: Context, memory, and knowledge framed as an engineered layer
beats.summary: A paper, an InfoQ architecture piece, and a Show HN tool all treat context selection and compression as a system component.

beats.headline: Evaluations probe whether models actually reason over retrieved knowledge
beats.summary: Work on multi-hop integration, multilingual relational reasoning, false-correction adoption, and private retrieval.

beats.headline: Retrieval mechanics move from similarity toward utility
beats.summary: Value-indexed traversal, linear-attention memory, distillation into weights, and utility-ranked recall.

open_questions: Does utility-ranked retrieval like Jetriever beat embedding search on a public agent-memory benchmark at comparable cost?
Will any agent framework or vector store ship graph or transition-aware memory as a default?
Do the knowledge-integration evaluations (ImplicitHop, KAD) get adopted as standard RAG regression tests?
Does distilling retrieved knowledge into weights reduce RAG serving cost in a production report?
